acceptance_condition.required_acceptance_condition: a universal or eventual pointwise theorem proving low-order base positivity and high-order signed-tail domination for all sufficiently large eligible even N in the named class

candidate.falsifier: A lifted row with positive full action but nonpositive low-order base, or an adverse high-order tail at least as large as the low-order base, breaks the support-order bridge as an eventual-threshold candidate on this holdout.
candidate.mechanism: Keep the exact support-size <= 2 split from the fixture and evaluate consecutive forward period-lifts of the same seven residues.  This changes the prime-pair masses while preserving the support-order dictionary and residue operator.
candidate.name: period-lift support-order threshold scout
candidate.prediction: If the support-order split is an eventual theorem target, forward period-lifts should retain low-order base positivity and high-order tail domination with more slack than the early tight fixture row.
candidate.smallest_test: Evaluate the first eight forward period-lifts of the seven original support-packet residues.

decision: The support-order bridge survives the first eight forward period-lifts of the original seven residues.  All 56 holdout rows are full-positive and low-order-base-positive, with no sign mismatches.  The tight low-order base is about 0.37397 at target 124886, much larger than the original tight base near 0.05371.  The worst adverse high-order tail consumes about 13.27% of its base on target 164926, far below the original 76.58% fixture stress.  On this lifted holdout only, even the disconnected high-order adverse envelope stays below every low-order base.  This supports an eventual-threshold hypothesis for the support-order split, but proves no threshold theorem and does not supply a non-circular analytic estimate.  Goldbach remains open.
status_boundary: finite period-lift holdout only; no eventual-threshold theorem, low-order base theorem, high-order tail domination theorem, q286 threshold theorem, strict-central Goldbach theorem, or Goldbach proof
